definition_en: sweet food from a plant, the seed-bearing part of a plant, or the result of work
core_image: 果盘里摆着苹果、香蕉和葡萄，颜色鲜亮
scene: 果盘里摆着苹果、香蕉和葡萄，颜色鲜亮。I eat fruit every day.
sceneCN: 这里 fruit 是「水果」（第 01 个义项）；句意是我每天吃水果。

senses.title: Fruit as food
senses.definition: sweet food that grows on a plant
senses.example: I eat fruit every day.
senses.why: Fruit comes from Latin fructus, 'produce, enjoyment', from frui 'to enjoy'; the word names the part of a plant that is good to eat.
senses.whyCN: fruit 源自拉丁语 fructus「出产、享受」，其动词 frui 意为「享用」；这个词指植物可食的部分。

senses.title: The seed-bearing part of a plant
senses.definition: the part of a plant that holds seeds
senses.definitionCN: 植物结出的含种子部分
senses.example: The tree bears fruit in autumn.
senses.why: Botany uses the same word for the part that holds seeds, whether or not it is sweet, because that is what the plant produces.
senses.whyCN: 植物学用同一个词指含种子的部分，不管甜不甜，因为那正是植物的出产。

senses.title: The result of effort
senses.definition: the result or reward of effort
senses.example: Their hard work bore fruit.
senses.why: Because fruit is what a plant brings forth, English uses it for what work brings forth, as in the fruit of long effort.
senses.whyCN: 因为果实是植物结出的东西，英语就用它指努力带来的结果，如 long effort 的成果。

items.cn: 拉丁语 frui 意为「享用、使用」。

items.en: French carried the word to English.
items.cn: 法语把这个词带入英语。

items.en: It named the sweet part of a plant.
items.cn: 它指植物可食的甜味部分。

items.en: English used it for results of work.

definition_en: causing laughter, strange, or slightly unwell
core_image: 同学讲了一个笑话，全班笑得趴在桌上
scene: 同学讲了一个笑话，全班笑得趴在桌上。She told a funny story.
sceneCN: 这里 funny 是「好笑的」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她讲了一个好笑的故事。

senses.title: Causing laughter
senses.definition: causing laughter
senses.example: She told a funny story.
senses.exampleCN: 她讲了一个好笑的故事。
senses.why: Funny is fun plus -y; fun first meant a joke or a diversion, so funny describes what produces that kind of amusement.
senses.whyCN: funny 是 fun 加 -y；fun 最初指玩笑或消遣，funny 就形容能产生这种乐趣的东西。

senses.title: Strange or hard to explain
senses.definition: strange or hard to explain
senses.example: There is a funny smell in the kitchen.
senses.why: Because something amusing can also be odd, the same word slid into 'strange', especially when a thing feels slightly wrong.
senses.whyCN: 因为引人发笑的东西也可能古怪，这个词又滑向「奇怪」，尤其当某物让人觉得不太对劲时。

senses.title: Slightly unwell
senses.definition: slightly unwell
senses.example: I feel funny after that ride.
senses.exampleCN: 坐完那趟车我有点不舒服。
senses.why: The 'odd' sense applies to how the body feels, so feel funny means feeling slightly ill or dizzy.
senses.whyCN: 「古怪」的意思也用于身体的感受，所以 feel funny 表示有点不舒服或发晕。

senses.title: The soft hair of an animal

scene: 课间操场上，孩子们分成两队玩抓人游戏。The children played a game.
sceneCN: 这里 game 是「游戏」（第 01 个义项）；句意是孩子们玩了一个游戏。

senses.title: An activity played for fun
senses.definition: an activity done for fun
senses.example: The children played a game.
senses.why: Old English gamen meant joy and amusement; the word named any activity people do for fun.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 gamen 意为「欢乐、消遣」；这个词指人们为取乐而做的活动。

senses.title: A single contest
senses.definition: one contest in a sport
senses.example: We won the game yesterday.
senses.why: Because a game has rules and a result, the same word names one contest within a sport, as in a football game.
senses.whyCN: 因为游戏有规则和结果，同一个词也指一项运动中的一场较量，如足球比赛。

senses.title: Wild animals hunted for food or sport
senses.definition: wild animals hunted for food or sport
senses.example: The forest is full of game.
senses.why: Hunting used the word for the animals chased, since the chase was the sport; that old sense survives in game as prey.
senses.whyCN: 狩猎用这个词指被追逐的动物，因为追逐本身就是这项活动；这个旧义保留在「猎物」上。

definition_en: a piece of ground for flowers, for vegetables, or around a house
core_image: 屋后的小花园里，玫瑰沿着木栅栏开花
scene: 屋后的小花园里，玫瑰沿着木栅栏开花。There are roses in the garden.
sceneCN: 这里 garden 是「花园」（第 01 个义项）；句意是花园里有玫瑰。

senses.title: A piece of ground where flowers grow
senses.definition: ground where flowers are grown
senses.example: There are roses in the garden.
senses.why: Garden comes from Old Northern French gardin, from a Germanic word for an enclosure; a garden is ground enclosed and tended.
senses.whyCN: garden 源自古北部法语 gardin，出自日耳曼语表示「围起来的地方」的词；花园就是围起来并加以照料的地。

senses.title: A plot where vegetables are grown
senses.definition: a plot where vegetables are grown
senses.example: We grow tomatoes in the vegetable garden.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在菜园里种西红柿。
senses.why: The same enclosed ground, when planted with food rather than flowers, is called a garden of vegetables.
senses.whyCN: 同一块围起来的地，若种的是吃的而不是花，就叫菜园。

senses.title: The ground around a house
senses.definition: the ground around a house
senses.example: The children play in the back garden.
senses.why: In British use the tended ground around a house is the garden, whether or not it has flowers.
senses.whyCN: 在英式用法里，房子周围经过照料的地都叫 garden，不管有没有花。

definition_en: something given to someone, or a natural ability
core_image: 生日桌上放着一个系着丝带的盒子，孩子双手接过来
scene: 生日桌上放着一个系着丝带的盒子，孩子双手接过来。She gave me a birthday gift.
sceneCN: 这里 gift 是「礼物」（第 01 个义项）；句意是她送了我一件生日礼物。

senses.title: Something given to someone
senses.definition: something given to someone
senses.example: She gave me a birthday gift.
senses.exampleCN: 她送了我一件生日礼物。
senses.why: Gift comes from Old Norse gift, related to give; it names the thing that is given rather than the act.
senses.whyCN: gift 源自古诺斯语 gift，与 give「给」同源；它指被给出的东西，而不是给这个动作。

senses.title: A natural ability
senses.definition: a natural ability
senses.example: He has a gift for music.
senses.why: Because a talent seems handed to a person rather than earned, English calls it a gift, as something given.
senses.whyCN: 因为才能像是被交到某人手上而不是挣来的，英语把它叫作 gift，即被给予的东西。

definition_zh: 手套；拳击手套；棒球手套
definition_en: a cover for the hand with separate fingers, or a padded hand cover used in sport
core_image: 雪地里，孩子戴着厚手套堆雪人
scene: 雪地里，孩子戴着厚手套堆雪人。Wear gloves in the cold.
sceneCN: 这里 glove 是「手套」（第 01 个义项）；句意是天冷要戴手套。

senses.title: A cover for the hand with separate fingers
senses.definition: a hand cover with separate fingers
senses.example: Wear gloves in the cold.
senses.why: Old English glof named a hand cover; the word is Germanic and its deeper origin is unknown.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 glof 指护手的用具；这个词属日耳曼语，更早的来源不明。

senses.title: A padded glove used in boxing
senses.definition: a padded glove worn in boxing
senses.example: He put on his boxing gloves.
senses.why: The padded mitt of boxing is a glove in the plain sense, enlarged and softened for hitting.
senses.whyCN: 拳击用的厚垫手套仍是本义的 glove，只是加大加软以便击打。

senses.title: A leather glove used to catch a ball
senses.definition: a leather glove used to catch a ball
senses.example: He caught the ball with his glove.
senses.exampleCN: 他用棒球手套接住了球。
senses.why: Baseball borrowed the everyday word for the leather hand cover that catches the ball.
senses.whyCN: 棒球借用了这个日常词，指接球用的皮革护手。
